<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par86" />Both these forms (''c'' and ''d'') indicate customary occupations, inhering in the subject, like Greek nouns in της, τεύς, e.g. πολίτης, γραμματεύς.

{{GHGmargin-letter|86|e}}
3. Nouns with {{GHGheb|text=מ‍}} prefixed, denoting the place where a thing is (cf. {{GHGpar|85|e}}), or its neighbourhood, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מַעְיָן|translate=a place of fountains}}, from {{GHGheb|text=עַ֫יִן}}; {{GHGheb|text=מַרְגְּלוֹת|translate=the place about the feet}}, {{GHGheb|text=מְרַֽאֲשׁוֹת|translate=the place about the head}}, from {{GHGheb|text=רֶ֫גֶל}}, {{GHGheb|text=רֹאשׁ}}; {{GHGheb|text=מִקְשָׁה}} (for {{GHGheb|text=מִקְשְׁאָה}}) ''a cucumber field'', from {{GHGheb|text=קִשֻּׁא|translate=cucumber}}. Cf. ἀμπελών from ἄμπελος.

{{GHGmargin-letter|86|f}}
4. Nouns with the termination {{GHGheb|text=־ָן}} or {{GHGheb|text=וֹן}} expressing adjectival ideas: {{GHGheb|text=קַדְמוֹן|translate=eastern}}, from {{GHGheb|text=קֶ֫דֶם}}; {{GHGheb|text=אַֽחֲרוֹן|translate=posterior}}, from {{GHGheb|text=אַחַר}}; {{GHGheb|text=חִיצוֹן|translate=exterior}}, from {{GHGheb|text=חוּץ}}; probably also {{GHGheb|text=לִוְיָתָן|translate=coiled}}, hence ''coiled animal, serpent'', from {{GHGheb|text=לִוְיָה|translate=a winding}}; {{GHGheb|text=נְחֻשְׁתָּן|translate=brazen}}, from {{GHGheb|text=נְחֹ֫שֶׁת|translate=brass}}. Also ''abstracts'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=עִוָּרוֹן|translate=blindness}}, from {{GHGheb|text=עִוֵּר}}. Cf. {{GHGpar|85|u}}.— With a double termination (''ôn'' or ''ân'' with ''î'') {{GHGheb|text=אַדְמֹנִי|translate=reddish}}, {{GHGheb|text=יִדְּעֹנִי|translate=a knowing}} (spirit); {{GHGheb|text=צִפְעֹנִי|translate=basilisk}}; {{GHGheb|text=רַֽחֲמָֽנִיּוֹת|translate=merciful}} [fem. plur.].

{{GHGmargin-letter|86|g}}
{{GHGheb|text=וֹן}} appears to be used as a diminutive ending (cf. the Syriac {{GHGheb|text=וּן}}) in {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁוֹן|translate=little man}} (in the eye), ''apple of the eye'', from {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ}}<ref>Cf. Barth, § 212; König, ii. 1, 413. Diminutives in Semitic languages are, however, most commonly formed by inserting a ''y'' after the second radical, e.g. Aram. {{GHGheb|text=עוּלֵּימָא}}, Syr. {{syriac|text=ܥܰܠܝܡܳܐ|font=western}}, Arab. {{arabic|غُ‍لَ‍يِّ‍مٌ}} {{GHGtranslate|a very young man, kulaib, a little dog}}, &c. Since Olshausen (§ 180), {{GHGheb|text=זְעֵיר|translate=a little}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=28|verse=10.13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=36|verse=2}}) has commonly been regarded as an example of the same form, to which others have added {{GHGheb|text=שְׁבִיסִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=3|verse=18}} (as though a foreign dialectical form for ''šumais'', {{GHGtranslate|little sun}}), and {{GHGheb|text=אֲמִינוֹן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=13|verse=20}}, as a contemptuous diminutive form of {{GHGheb|text=אַמְנוֹן}}; cf. Ewald, § 167, W. Wright, ''Arab. Gramm.''<sup>2</sup> i. § 269, De Lagarde, {{GHGcite|title=Nominalbildung}}, pp. 85–87, König. ii. 1, p. 143 f. The existence of the form in Hebrew is disputed by Barth, § 192 ''d''.]</ref>; on the other hand {{GHGheb|text=שְׁפִיפֹן|translate=adder}}, which was formerly regarded as a diminutive, is properly an adjectival form from {{GHGheb|text=שָׁפַף|translate=to rub}} (hence, as it were, a ''rubbing'' creature); in the same way {{GHGheb|text=יְשֻׁרוּן}} is a ''denominative'' from {{GHGheb|text=יָשׁוּר}} (={{GHGheb|text=יָשָׁר}}), properly ''upright'' (''righteous people''), and not a ''diminutive'' (''pious little people'', and the like); finally, {{GHGheb|text=שַֽׂהֲרוֹן}} is not ''lunula'', but ''an artificial moon'' (used as an ornament), and {{GHGheb|text=צַוְּרֹנִים}} not ''little neck'', but ''necklace'' (from {{GHGheb|text=צַוָּאר|translate=neck}}). Cf. Delitzsch on {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=4|verse=9}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|86|h}}
5. Peculiar to denominatives is the termination {{GHGheb|text=־ִי}}, which converts a substantive into an adjective, and is added especially to numerals and names of persons and countries, in order to form ''ordinals, patronymics'', and ''tribal names''; e.g. {{GHGheb|text=רַגְלִי|translate=footman}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=רַגְלִים}}, from {{GHGheb|text=רֶ֫גֶל|translate=foot}}; {{GHGheb|text=אַכְזָרִי|translate=cruel}}, {{GHGheb|text=נָכְרִי|translate=strange}}, from {{GHGheb|text=נֹ֫כֶר|translate=strangeness}}, {{GHGheb|text=תַּחְתִּי|translate=lower}}, from {{GHGheb|text=תַּ֫חַת|translate=below}}, fem. {{GHGheb|text=תָּחְתִּית}} and {{GHGheb|text=תַּחְתִּיָּה}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=תַּחְתִּיִּים}}, {{GHGheb|text=תַּחְתִּיּוֹת}}; {{GHGheb|text=שִׁשִּׁי|translate=the sixth}}, from {{GHGheb|text=שֵׁשׁ|translate=six}}; {{GHGheb|text=מֽוֹאָבִי|translate=Moabite}}, from {{GHGheb|text=מוֹאָב}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=מֹֽאָבִים}}, fem. {{GHGheb|text=מֽוֹאֲבִיָּה}} and {{GHGheb|text=מֽוֹאָבִית}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=מֽוֹאֲבִיּוֹת}}; {{GHGheb|text=עִבְרִי|translate=Hebrew}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=עִבְרִים}} and {{GHGheb|text=עִבְרִיִּים}}, fem. {{GHGheb|text=עִבְרִיָּה}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=עִבְרִיּוֹת}}; {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׂרְאֵלִי|translate=Israelite}}, from {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׂרָאֵל}}. When the original substantive is a ''compound'', it is resolved again into two words, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בֶּן־יְמִינִי|translate=Benjamite}}, from {{GHGheb|text=בִּנְיָמִין}} (cf. on the use of the article in such cases, {{GHGpar|127|d}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|86|i}}
Instead of {{GHGheb|text=־ִי}} we find in a few cases (''a'') the ending {{GHGheb|text=־ַי}} (as in Aram.), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=כִּילַי}} (''crafty'', or, according to others, ''churlish'') if it stands for {{GHGheb|text=נְכִילַי}} and is not rather from a stem {{GHGheb|text=כלא}} or {{GHGheb|text=כלה}}; {{GHGheb|text=חוֹרָי|translate=white cloth}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=19|verse=9}} in pause; perhaps also {{GHGheb|text=גֹּבַי|translate=a swarm of locusts}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=7|verse=1}} ({{GHGheb|text=גּוֹבָ֑י}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=3|verse=17}}); hardly {{GHGheb|text=נְגִֽינוֹתַי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=38|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=3|verse=19}}; but certainly in proper names as {{GHGheb|text=בַּרְזִלַּי}} (''ferreus'') ''Barzillai'';<ref>On {{GHGheb|text=־ַי}} as an old fem. ending, see above, {{GHGpar|80|l}}.</ref> and (''b'') {{GHGheb|text=־ֶה}},<section end="par86" /><noinclude>
